_meta.description: Whether a RISE customer can actually produce each logical source, in five states rather than the two the coverage manifest used to have.
_meta.why_two_states_was_not_enough: Coverage had one set, RISE_UNREACHABLE_SOURCES, holding five OS-level sources. Everything else absent was reported as 'missing' — the customer forgot it. But docs/RISE_SECURITY_MODEL.md section 3 already classified the upload surface in FIVE states, and eleven sources it calls SAP-operated were being counted against the customer. Telling a RISE customer they failed to export what SAP contractually operates is the same defect the original set was created to prevent, left half-finished.

states.yes: Customer self-serves. Absent means they did not send it.
states.read_only: Customer can export it but cannot remediate what it shows. Absent is still theirs to fix; the FINDING is not.
states.partial: Obtainable but incomplete or mixed-ownership. What arrives will not be the whole picture, and a check reading it must say so. Two do: system_trust states the clients its standard-user result covers (STDUSR-COV-001), and server/enrich.py classifies each RFC destination's operator. The coverage manifest also lists every supplied partial source, so one that no check qualifies is still visible as qualified.
states.ticket: Not self-servable. The customer must raise an SAP service request. Absent is NOT a customer failure.
states.no: Structurally unavailable. No amount of customer effort produces it.

_meta.how_absence_is_triaged: yes / read_only / partial -> missing (the customer can obtain it). ticket -> needs_sap_action. no -> unreachable. The middle bucket is the one that did not exist before, and it is the whole point: 'ask SAP for it' is neither 'you forgot' nor 'impossible'.
_meta.the_default_for_an_unlisted_source: missing, which is the behaviour that was there before. Most of the 139 sources are application-layer and customer-owned, so defaulting to 'you can get this' is right for the majority AND is the conservative direction: it asks for data rather than excusing its absence. The count of unclassified sources is reported so the gap stays visible instead of being absorbed by the default.
_meta.on_premise: Not consulted at all. Outside RISE the customer owns every layer, so the question does not arise — the same test server/enrich.py and modules/coverage.py already use (deployment_modes.is_rise).
_meta.provenance: Transcribed from docs/RISE_SECURITY_MODEL.md section 3, 'What evidence a RISE customer can actually produce', whose rows carry their own [SAP-primary] markers. Rows where one table line covers several loader keys are marked `grouping: derived` with the sentence that licenses the split. Nothing here is a new judgement about SAP's contract.
open_questions: HANA parameter/encryption/audit-policy system views: section 8 records 'Can a CUST_USER_ROLE_ADMIN holder read HANA parameter system views?' as UNRESOLVED, to be tested on a design-partner tenant. They are marked `ticket` rather than `no` because 'ask SAP' is true under either answer, while `no` would assert the stronger claim section 8 says we cannot make. Marked verified: false so the answer can be filled in rather than rediscovered.
sources: docs/RISE_SECURITY_MODEL.md section 8 (open questions gating the HANA rows)

security_params.how: Report RSPARAM / RSPFPAR; RZ11 per parameter; TU02 for change history
security_params.blocked_by: SAP executes parameter maintenance. KBA 3460793 documents the customer unable to save in RZ10.
security_params.note: Exportable, not fixable. server/enrich.py already routes PARAM-* findings to ticket_to_sap.

client_settings.blocked_by: Global change and default client settings are SAP-executed

icf_services.blocked_by: Deactivating critical ICF services appears as an SAP Standard task — the finding is real, the fix is a ticket

standard_users.blocked_by: Cross-client by nature; client 000 access is restricted and on-request, so a customer may only evidence productive clients.
standard_users.note: Section 3.1: a cross-client check must never silently pass on partial data. Enforced by modules/client_scope.py — STDUSR-002 and STDUSR-003 carry the clients they were computed over and STDUSR-COV-001 names the ones they did not reach.

rfc_destinations.blocked_by: Mixed ownership — the export contains SAP-managed technical and monitoring destinations the customer must not touch.
rfc_destinations.note: Obtainable in full; it is the OWNERSHIP that is partial. server/enrich.py:classify_destination_owner is the pass that sorts them.

hana_db_users.blocked_by: Scoped to non-technical users; technical and admin users are SAP's

hana_parameters.open_question: Whether a CUST_USER_ROLE_ADMIN holder can read the parameter system views was not verified — section 8 gates this on a design-partner tenant.

hana_version.licence: Not named separately in section 3; grouped with the HANA parameter rows because it is the same system-view access question. If the design-partner test says parameters are readable, this moves with them.

tls_config.licence: Section 3's TLS/SNC/crypto row: 'ICM/SNC parameters and the crypto library are SAP-operated.'

crypto_library.licence: Section 3's TLS/SNC/crypto row is rated Partial and explains the split itself: 'Certificate and PSE inventory reachable; ICM/SNC parameters and the crypto library are SAP-operated.'

ucon_rfc_state.note: The R&R explicitly puts business-client UCON configuration with the customer, and this is the ABAP-layer stand-in for the gateway ACL files they cannot reach.

webdisp_params.how: The Web Dispatcher instance profile, as a NAME,VALUE list
webdisp_params.blocked_by: SAP operates the Web Dispatcher in a RISE tenant, so the profile is theirs to export and theirs to change
webdisp_params.note: MIXED BY TOPOLOGY, and `ticket` is the safer half. A customer running their OWN dispatcher in front of the tenant can export it freely and these findings are directly actionable for them; where SAP operates it, absence is a service request rather than a forgotten export. Classified `ticket` because that never blames the customer for SAP's component, and a customer who does own theirs simply supplies it.
